es.summary: Recién nacido antes de cumplir las 37 semanas de gestación. Tiene más riesgo de problemas respiratorios, hipotermia, hipoglucemia e infección.
key_points: Se considera pretérmino todo RN nacido antes de la semana 37.
Subgrupos: pretérmino tardío (34 a 36 semanas), moderado (32 a 34), muy pretérmino (menos de 32) y extremo (28 semanas o menos).
Riesgo principal: síndrome de dificultad respiratoria por déficit de surfactante.
Le cuesta regular la temperatura porque tiene poca grasa parda y glucógeno.
Los corticoides prenatales (betametasona) a la madre mejoran la madurez pulmonar.

usage: Se combina con la clasificación por peso: RNPAEG (pretérmino adecuado), RNPEG (pequeño), RNPGEG (grande).
Ejemplo: «RNP de 34 semanas por Ballard, peso 2 100 g».
Se usa también para anotar la causa: «RNP por APP» o «RNP por RPM».
nursing_care: Vigilar la respiración: aleteo nasal, quejido, tiraje y saturación.
Mantener la termorregulación (incubadora o contacto piel con piel).
Controlar la glucemia y la tolerancia a la alimentación (succión y deglución inmaduras).
Vigilar ictericia, apneas y signos de infección.
Apoyar a la familia y promover el vínculo y la extracción de leche materna.

en.summary: A newborn born before 37 weeks of gestation (RNP in Spanish). Preterm babies are at higher risk of breathing problems, low body temperature, low blood sugar and infection.
key_points: A newborn born before the start of the 37th week of gestation is preterm.
Subcategories: late preterm (34 to 36 weeks), moderately preterm (32 to 34), very preterm (less than 32) and extremely preterm (28 weeks or less).
Main risk: respiratory distress syndrome due to a lack of pulmonary surfactant.
Thermoregulation is difficult because brown fat and glycogen stores are not fully developed.
Antenatal steroids (betamethasone) given to the mother improve fetal lung maturity.

usage: Combined with the weight classification: RNPAEG (preterm AGA), RNPEG (preterm SGA), RNPGEG (preterm LGA).
Example: "RNP 34 weeks by Ballard, weight 2,100 g".
Also used to record the cause: "RNP due to preterm labor (APP)" or "due to PROM (RPM)".
nursing_care: Watch breathing: nasal flaring, grunting, retractions and oxygen saturation.
Monitor blood glucose and feeding tolerance (immature sucking and swallowing).
Watch for jaundice, apnea and signs of infection.
Support the family and encourage bonding and breast milk expression.

summary.0.quote: A newborn born before the start of the 37th week of gestation is prete

key_points.0.quote: A newborn born before the start of the 37th week of gestation is prete

key_points.1.quote: The subcategories of prematurity are late preterm , born between 34 and 36 completed weeks of pregnancy; moderately preterm , born between 32 and 34 weeks of pregnancy; very preterm , born at less than 32 weeks of pregnancy; and extremely preterm , born at or before 28 weeks of pregnancy (Mayo Foundation for Medical Education and Research [MFMER], 2021).

key_points.2.quote: All premature infants (sometimes called preemies) are at risk for respiratory difficulties called respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) due to immature lungs.

key_points.3.quote: In addition, thermoregulation in the newborn relies on brown fat and glycogen availability in the liver, and these are not fully developed until the end of the third trimester.

key_points.4.quote: Treatment with antenatal steroids, exogenous surfactant, caffeine, and/or continuous positive airway pressure improves lung function and decreases the clinical course for the patient (Martin, 2023).

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: The newborn will have tachypnea, nasal flaring, expiratory grunting, and multilevel retractions, as the rib cage is primarily cartilaginous at this age.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: The infant is placed under a warmer or in a clear, heated box called an incubator, which regulates the air temperature.
